input: ADC counts (0..1023, state.lookup_input) of sensor channel 3 = the barometric pressure sensor (channel_index 3; config block barometric_pressure_sensor_config; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel0_init)
output: sensor_channel3_value (0x40bd82) = barometric pressure at 1/18.56 kPa per count, also sensor_channel_filtered_output[3] = sensor_readings_t.barometric_pressure; J1939 AMB SPN 108; cm848_calculateBoostPressure and cm848_processEngineOilPressure subtract it; barometric_pressure_sensor_config.default_value (1132) is the fallback
units_check: ADC 102..922 (0.5..4.5 V) maps linearly 832..2048 counts = 44.8..110.3 kPa, flat outside (breakpoints 41/61/82 and 942/963/983 are extra clamp points); config thresholds high 993 / low 51 (ADC); RAM dump slot 3 reads 1647 = 88.7 kPa, which is ADC about 652 = 3.2 V, plausible for a 45..110 kPa absolute sensor
evidence: The config block is already named barometric_pressure_sensor_config; fault bits 25/26 decode (ROM 0x5985a -> obd_dtc_code_table) to P0108 / P0107; the firmware/CLAUDE.md identity table proves slot 3 = AMB SPN 108.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 9 = intake manifold temperature (channel_index 9; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel10_intakeManifoldTemperatureInit)
output: sensor_channel9_pressure_value (0x40bd86) = intake manifold temperature at 1/64 deg F per count; slot 9 = intake_manifold_temperature_sensor_filtered, sent as J1939 IC1 SPN 105 and copied to intake_manifold_temperature_in_use
units_check: ADC 12..945 maps 17024..-3200 counts = 266..-50 deg F (falling NTC-type curve, signed data flag 2); ADC 0..11 gives 7360 = 115 deg F = the config default; config thresholds high 1002 / low 12; dump slot 9 reads 2601 = 40.6 deg F
evidence: The wrapper is already named ...intakeManifoldTemperatureInit (reviewed 2026-11-13); fault bits 19/20 decode to P0113 / P0112 (intake air temperature circuit high / low); identity table slot 9 = IC1 SPN 105.
naming_concern: destination sensor_channel9_pressure_value (0x40bd86) and sensor_channel9_pressure_default_value (0x40bd9e) are misnamed 'pressure': they hold the intake manifold temperature in 1/64 deg F.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 10 = engine oil pressure (channel_index 10; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel11_init)
output: sensor_channel10_value (0x40bd8c) = engine oil pressure at 1/18.56 kPa per count (absolute coding); slot 10 = oil_pressure_sensor_filtered, sent as J1939 EFL/P1 SPN 100 and PCI 0xC0 byte 2; cm848_processEngineOilPressure subtracts barometric_pressure
units_check: ADC 102..921 (0.5..4.5 V) maps 832..13632 counts = 44.8..734.5 kPa absolute, flat outside; config default 12800 (a high fallback), thresholds high 988 / low 68; dump slot 10 reads 832 = the low clamp with the engine stopped
evidence: The firmware/CLAUDE.md identity table proves slot 10 = oil pressure (SPN 100, PCI 0xC0 byte 2) and the 832 dump value with the engine stopped equals this table's floor; the channel has no OBD-II code (fault bits 12/13 map to the no-code slot).

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 8 (channel_index 8; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel12_init; fault bits 77 / 78)
output: sensor_channel8_value (0x40bddc); slot 8 is the global named governor_torque_output (0x40bb00): cm848_buildPgn61443ElectronicEngineController2Message sends it as EEC2 byte 4 'remote accelerator position' (counts x 0.625 = 0.4 %/bit, SPN 974) and fuel_demandRateLimit_outputCheck compares it with fuel_demand_control_t.rate_limited
units_check: ADC 0..1023 maps linearly 0..400 counts = 0..100 % at 0.25 %/count (evenly spaced breakpoints 0,146,...,1023 -> 0,57,...,400); the EEC2 byte is counts x 0.625 = 250 at 100 %, correct for 0.4 %/bit; config default 0, thresholds high 1000 / low 100; dump reads 0
evidence: The EEC2 builder sends the byte only when system_feature_config_flags bit 12 is set and bits 0x2000 / 0x4000 of fault_detected_bits_64_to_79 (fault bits 77 / 78) are clear, which are exactly this channel's high / low fault bits (0x4d / 0x4e); fuel_demandRateLimit_outputCheck tests fault bit 78 next to this value.
naming_concern: global governor_torque_output (0x40bb00 = sensor_channel_filtered_output[8]) is misnamed: it is the remote accelerator pedal position (0.25 %/count); sensor_channel8_value carries the same signal.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 13 = the accelerator pedal (channel_index 13; config accelerator_pedal_sensor_config; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel13_init)
output: sensor_channel13_value (0x40bde0); slot 13 = accelerator_pedal_sensor_filtered at 0.25 %/count (400 = 100 %), read by cm848_fuelDemandBaseCalculation and cm848_fuelDemandFinalCalculation; the J1939 pedal can replace it through sensor_channel13_ram.held_value
units_check: ADC 39..839 (0.19..4.10 V) maps 0..400 counts = 0..100 %; 400 held to ADC 866, then 0 from ADC 867 (high-side fault region reads idle); config thresholds high 840 / low 64, default 0; dump slot 13 reads 27 = 6.8 % at rest
evidence: The config is named accelerator_pedal_sensor_config; fault bits 10/11 decode to P2123 / P2122 (pedal position sensor circuit high / low); identity table slot 13 = accelerator_pedal_sensor_filtered.
naming_concern: fault_detected_bits_336_to_351 also names P2122 / P2123 / P2127 / P2128 (bits 347..350), so a second pedal channel or path may exist elsewhere; this table is channel 13 = accelerator_pedal_sensor_filtered (fault bits 10 / 11).

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 42 (channel_index 42; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel14_init), the monitor of the 5 V sensor reference supply A
output: sensor_channel42_value (0x40bde4) = supply voltage at 1/1024 V per count; no function reads the value or slot 42, its use is the channel's own range check (config thresholds in ADC counts) raising fault bits 338 / 337
units_check: ADC 0..1023 maps 0..6144 counts (6.006 per ADC count) = 0..6.0 V at 1/1024 V per count; config default 5120 = 5.000 V; thresholds high 942 (5.52 V) / low 711 (4.17 V); dump slot 42 reads 5135 = 5.01 V
evidence: Fault bits 338 / 337 decode (ROM 0x5985a -> obd_dtc_code_table) to P0643 / P0642 = Sensor Reference Voltage A circuit high / low; the config default 5120 and the dump value 5135 both equal 5 V at 1/1024 V per count.
naming_concern: A and C are the SAE J2012 letters of P0642/P0643 and P0698/P0699, the physical supply numbering is not established; sensor_channel42_value is generic and no global carries the role.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 20 = ambient air temperature (channel_index 20; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel1_init)
output: sensor_channel20_value (0x40bd90); slot 20 = ambient_air_temperature_sensor_filtered at 1/64 deg F per count, sent as J1939 AMB SPN 171
units_check: ADC 41..978 maps 17024..-2560 counts = 266..-40 deg F (falling NTC-type curve, signed data flag 2); config default 10240 = 160 deg F, thresholds high 1002 / low 20; dump slot 20 reads 2260 = 35.3 deg F (cold dump, matches the existing note)

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 77 (channel_index 77; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel4_init); the sensor is not identified
output: unnamed WORD_003fa046 (value), WORD_003fa048 (default), WORD_003fa04a (status) and slot 77 = governor_integrator_bound_a (0x40bb8a): cm848_checkSensorDeviationFlags compares it with barometric_pressure and with governor_integrator_bound_b (0x40bb3c) at cranking, fuel_egrTarget_pressureRatio_calc divides it by fuel_pressure_sensor_reference
units_check: ADC 102..921 maps 754..6585 counts = 40.6..354.8 kPa at 1/18.56 kPa per count, exactly the MAP curve boost_pressure_linearization (754 / 6585); dump slot 77 reads 1703 beside MAP 1700 and barometric 1647 (all atmospheric, engine stopped); config default 0, thresholds 1023 / 0 (no range fault)
evidence: An absolute pressure sensor of the same type as the MAP, cross-checked against barometric pressure, but what it measures is not named anywhere. N in the base is the channel_index 77 (as in sensor_channel77_*), not the wrapper ordinal 4. The name itself is certain (channel_index is a literal call argument); medium only means the sensor is not identified.
naming_concern: slot 77 global governor_integrator_bound_a (0x40bb8a) and governor_integrator_bound_b (0x40bb3c, slot 38) are sensor-array pressures, not governor integrator bounds; the 'egr' / iat_sensor_deviation_flags names around their consumers look misdomained; WORD_003fa046 / 8 / a are this channel's value / default / status.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 105 (channel_index 105; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel5_init); the sensor is not identified
output: sensor_channel105_value (0x40bd84) -> boost_sensor_raw_input in cm848_updateFaultStatusRegisters, which filters it (boost_pressure_fault_filter_state) and forms sensor_channel105_pressure_diff = value - filtered; cm848_selectFaultProtectionValue then passes either that difference or sensor_channel105_default_value to boost_pressure_correction_raw
units_check: if 1/18.56 kPa per count (the unit is not proven for this channel): ADC 102..921 maps -32..640 counts = -1.7..34.5 kPa, a low-range gauge or differential span rather than a boost range; signed data flag 2; RAM-resident table (0x3feee2); config default 0, thresholds high 1003 / low 20; dump slot 105 reads 0
evidence: Input is the channel's ADC counts and the output is sensor_channel105_value, but the consumer chain is a fault filter whose boost_* names do not fit a -1.7..34.5 kPa span, so the sensor is not certain. N in the base is the channel_index 105, not the wrapper ordinal 5. The name itself is certain (channel_index is a literal call argument); medium only means the sensor is not identified.
naming_concern: consumer names boost_sensor_raw_input / boost_pressure_fault_filter_state / boost_pressure_correction_raw / governor_speed_output_limit (= channel 105 fault status | boost fault flag) probably do not describe a boost signal.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 69 = the battery temperature thermistor (channel_index 69; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel69_init)
output: sensor_channel69_value (0x40bd92); slot 69 = battery_temperature_sensor_filtered at 1/64 deg F per count, sets the charging voltage target and goes out in PCI 0xC0 byte 4
units_check: ADC 41..992 maps 18176..-1408 counts = 284..-22 deg F (falling NTC-type curve, signed data flag 2), the documented curve -22 to 284 F; config default 3840 = 60 deg F (the documented default), thresholds high 1018 / low 27; dump slot 69 reads 2086 = 32.6 deg F

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 108 (channel_index 108; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel6_init); a temperature sensor of unidentified service
output: sensor_channel108_value (0x40bd94); slot 108 (DAT_0040bbc8, unnamed) is read only by cm848_calibration_group21_load_cont, which sets bits of engine_sync_validation_flags at cranking when coolant temperature < 6400 (100 deg F), coolant minus battery temperature < 640 (10 deg F) and DAT_00409eb0 (9600 = 150 deg F) < slot 108
units_check: ADC 19..1013 maps 36608..896 counts = 572..14 deg F at 1/64 deg F per count (falling curve with a hot span); the call passes flags 0 = unsigned interpolation, but the only reader loads slot 108 as a signed halfword, so the first two points (ADC 19 / 25 = 36608 / 34304) exceed the signed range and sit at or just above the config low-fault threshold 19, i.e. they are not live readings; RAM-resident table (0x3fef22); config default 4608 = 72 deg F, thresholds high 1019 / low 19; dump slot 108 reads 4608 = the default (no live sensor)
evidence: The 1/64 deg F unit is fixed by the consumer comparing it with coolant / battery temperature thresholds (6400 / 640 / 9600) and by the curve shape; what the sensor measures is not named anywhere. N in the base is the channel_index 108, not the wrapper ordinal 6. The name itself is certain (channel_index is a literal call argument); medium only means the sensor is not identified.
naming_concern: slot 108 (0x40bbc8) is unnamed; cm848_calibration_group21_load_cont and engine_sync_validation_flags read like a cold-start temperature plausibility check, not calibration loading or engine sync.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 88 (channel_index 88; Bank 2 wrapper cm848_sensorChannel7_init_configBundle @ 0x50011c); the sensor is not identified
output: disassembly of 0x50011c shows it writes the SAME three outputs as the fuel temperature wrapper cm848_sensorChannel9_init: value 0x40bdd0 (sensor_channel7_value), default 0x40bdd2, status 0x40be3a, plus its own slot 88 (0x40bba0, no direct reader)
units_check: ADC 0..1023 maps 12800..-12800 counts (signed data flag 2): +200..-200 if 1/64 deg F; near linear (about -0.32 deg F per ADC count from ADC 168 = 134 F to ADC 778 = -58 F) with steep clamps at both ends, not an NTC curve; config default 9216 (144 if 1/64 deg F), thresholds 1023 / 0 (no range fault); dump slot 88 reads 9216 = the default (no live sensor)
evidence: Input is the channel's ADC counts and the output is a named variable, but the output is shared with channel 7 and the unit is not proven, so only the channel number is certain. The base uses channel_index 88 because wrapper ordinal 7 already names sensor_channel7_linearization_* (0x59456, cm848_sensorChannel7_init). The name itself is certain (channel_index is a literal call argument); medium only means the sensor is not identified.
naming_concern: sensor_channel7_value / sensor_channel7_default_value / sensor_channel7_fault_status are written by both channel 7 (fuel temperature) and channel 88; two rows named sensor_channel7_fault_status exist (0x40be18 and 0x40be3a); the existing sensor_channel7_linearization_* table (0x59456) belongs to wrapper ordinal 7 = channel 75 (governor speed input), not to channel 7.

input: ADC counts of sensor channel 7 = fuel temperature (channel_index 7; wrapper cm848_sensorChannel9_init)
output: sensor_channel7_value (0x40bdd0); slot 7 = fuel_temperature_sensor_filtered at 1/64 deg F per count, sent as J1939 ET1 SPN 174 and stored in the freeze frame (fault_entry_t.fuel_temperature)
units_check: ADC 68..1001 maps 18176..-2560 counts = 284..-40 deg F (falling NTC-type curve, signed data flag 2; ADC 60 gives 12160 = 190 deg F as a clamp point); config default 4608 = 72 deg F, thresholds high 1000 / low 100; dump slot 7 reads 4608 = the default
evidence: The identity table in firmware/CLAUDE.md proves slot 7 = fuel temperature (ET1 SPN 174, from the ECM's own broadcast); the channel has no OBD-II code (fault bits 47/48 map to the no-code slot).
